name: PT Apollo Global Interactive Tbk

frontmatter.title: Apollo Global Interactive: the third quarter confirms the run-rate, the price still does not follow
frontmatter.summary: The 2026 third-quarter pack leaves the story where it was: a regional Honda dealer whose revenue keeps shrinking while the national market grows, thin earnings, a net cash balance sheet, and a controlling shareholder whose own tender valued the equity at a fraction of the quote. We keep SELL with a target of Rp75 against Rp1,850, a total return of -95.9%.
thesis: The company is a dealer, not a franchise. Revenue is the sale of Honda cars and spare parts plus a small operating-lease book, and one supplier accounts for more than half of consolidated revenue [S12]. Unit economics are set by the principal, not by the company.

Trading has decoupled from the business. The stock re-rated on a name change, a new controlling shareholder and a small distribution acquisition, while revenue fell -46.7% in FY2025 and a further -27.1% in our forecast, even as national wholesales rose 679,020 units over nine months [S13][S9].

{'The most likely path is stabilisation, not a return to the old peak': 'services and operating leases now carry the gross margin, vehicle volume is structurally challenged by Chinese brands, and the acquired Chery franchise is small and itself shrinking [S10][S13].'}

Our DCF, on a 11.9% WACC with a terminal value that is 46.1% of the total, gives Rp81, just below the hard-asset floor of land at cost plus net cash; the EV/EBITDA cross-check gives Rp56 and P/E Rp5, both struck on a trough trailing year. We do not use P/B because the peer median is above the asset-heavy comparables and the book it would capitalise is one we judge overstated. The gap to the quote is not a modelling artefact.

{'Governance is the reason we would not own this even at a fair multiple': 'the regulator fined three former directors for misleading financial statements, the asset line at the centre of that finding is still on the balance sheet, and the controlling shareholder bought in at a fraction of the current price [S3][S11][S12].'}

catalysts.event: FY2026 fourth-quarter and full-year financial statements, the first clean read on the post-refinancing capital structure
FY2026 audited results and annual report, including any follow-up on the regulator's finding
First full year of consolidation of the Chery distributor acquisition and its volume contribution
Year-end share register and any change in the controlling stake, the free float or the listing status

blocks.text: **We reiterate SELL with a target of Rp75 against a last price of Rp1,850, a total return of -95.9% with no dividend in the forecast [S13].** A results update on the 2026 third-quarter pack, not a change of view: the nine-month accounts match our initiation, and the quarter split only reshapes FY2026E, the fourth quarter held at the third-quarter run-rate [S13][S0]. The target is fundamental value, not a twelve-month forecast — the model cannot produce today's quote from any revenue path it will solve.

PT Apollo Global Interactive Tbk, until January 2026 PT Bintang Oto Global Tbk, is a Honda dealership group in Malang with used-car retail, a workshop, an operating-lease fleet and rental in East Java and Bali [S14][S7]; nine-month revenue was IDR206.8bn on vehicle sales of IDR137.9bn, earning IDR45.8bn of gross profit and IDR4.1bn of net profit [S13].

The price is not about the business. At Rp1,850 the equity is capitalised at IDR7,036.5bn against book equity of IDR461.3bn, on IDR1.1bn a day [S12][S0]. Three events coincided with the re-rating — the November 2025 change of control by GX Archipelago Pte Ltd [S14], the January 2026 renaming and new board [S12] and the IDR4.8bn Chery purchase [S2] — none changing the earning power of a dealer whose revenue fell from IDR901.8bn to IDR361.6bn in two years [S14][S12]. The controller paid Rp520 a share and offered Rp529 in the tender [S11] while the float now pays several times that — a pattern that usually prices an asset injection, but none is disclosed [S2][S13], so the base case excludes it and the risks section sizes it as the principal upside risk.

**What moves the value.** The revenue trajectory — stabilisation or continued share loss to Chinese brands — carries roughly half the range; the gross margin, up from 6.7% to 21.3% on mix, reverses if volume returns [S12][S13]; and the cost of capital, which is the house WACC at 11.9% with no company-specific premium added — the reporting-integrity finding is carried by the SELL rating, not by a wider discount rate [S3].

PT Apollo Global Interactive Tbk is an automotive group in Malang, East Java. It reports three segments — vehicles and spare parts, operating leases, and a residual bucket absorbing holding-company financing costs — and runs a Honda dealership, used-car retail, a workshop and an auto-rental fleet [S12][S14].

Revenue was IDR361.6bn in FY2025 against IDR901.8bn two years earlier, leases contributing IDR30.2bn [S12]; nine-month revenue was IDR206.8bn against IDR300.5bn, with vehicle sales of IDR137.9bn and leases of IDR23.8bn carrying almost all of it [S13]. The lease book is the most profitable asset, with a gross margin above half against less than a tenth for vehicles and parts, which is why a shrinking revenue line has produced a rising blended margin [S12].

The supply side is the structural fact. One supplier, PT Istana Mobil Surabaya Indah, was 53.4% of consolidated revenue in FY2025 [S12] and 58.2% in the nine months to September 2026 against 64.0% a year earlier [S13]: it buys from one distributor and resells in a territory, the manufacturer setting price and allocation. No customer reaches a tenth of revenue [S13].

The footprint is regional and shrinking: 6 operational areas and 145 employees at end-FY2025, down from 229 [S14]. It owns 18,899 square metres of land in Malang, Klaten, Bali, Madiun and Probolinggo, carried at IDR217.6bn of cost — close to half of book equity, not depreciated, which is why the equity is not worthless [S12].

Control changed in November 2025, when GX Archipelago Pte Ltd acquired 29.5% from PT Falcon Asia Investama, leaving 70.5% public and triggering a mandatory tender in early 2026 at Rp529 [S14][S11]. In January 2026 the company renamed itself and replaced its board; in November 2026 it bought PT Pradipta Cakra Buana, a Chery distributor, for IDR4.8bn [S2][S12]. The logic is legible — a second, Chinese brand alongside Honda — but immaterial at this size, and the brand is shrinking in Indonesia [S10].

The Indonesian car market is an oligopoly of Japanese principals distributing through appointed dealers
who own the land, showroom and workshop. The dealer earns a fixed percentage of the invoice plus a share
of service and parts revenue, so the principal captures the upside in a good year while the dealer
carries the fixed cost in a bad one. Franchise agreements are territorial and terminable, which is why
dealer groups trade at a discount to the brands they sell.

The domestic market is in an upswing this company has missed. National wholesales reached 679,020 units in the first nine months of 2026, up a fifth, September more than a quarter ahead [S9]. That rules out the company's own explanation — its FY2025 account blames weak demand [S14], defensible in a soft 2025 but not in 2026, when nine-month revenue fell roughly a third in a growing market [S13][S9]: the Honda franchise is losing ground, the dealer is ceding volume, or both.

Japanese brands still lead, but Chinese manufacturers are materially competitive, BYD the largest [S14]. It has also pulled the prospective second brand down: Chery's wholesales fell by nearly half in the nine months of 2026 to 8,313 units, with share roughly halving [S10]. It is buying distribution for a brand losing distribution faster than the market is growing.

Market position is that of a small regional challenger: at IDR361.6bn of revenue it is a rounding error nationally, its East Java position the only defensible asset, held by land and a franchise rather than anything it controls [S12][S9]. Supplier power is high — one distributor supplies more than half the revenue line and sets price and allocation [S12]; buyer power is rising as customers compare a Honda against a cheaper Chinese alternative [S14]; new entrants arrive as Chinese brands appointing their own dealers, the channel the company has just bought into [S10]; rivalry is intense, a territorial franchise protecting the territory but not the customer.

There is no moat — a licence-like relationship, a piece of land and a service base; the house method asks whether growth is manufactured by reinvestment at high incremental returns, and here it is allocated by a principal, which is why we value faded cash flows rather than a compounding story [S9]. External influences are second-order: the rupiah and policy rate affect inventory funding and customers' instalments more than a company earning and spending in rupiah [S12], while manufacturer incentives — a meaningful revenue line in 2025, nearly gone a year later — explain part of the margin move [S13].

**2026 third-quarter results.** The nine-month accounts came in on our initiation's trajectory: revenue IDR206.8bn against IDR300.5bn a year earlier, gross profit IDR45.8bn, net profit IDR4.1bn [S13]. The pack shows the sequential decline flattening sharply into the third quarter [S0], so we hold the fourth at that run-rate, lifting FY2026E revenue to IDR263.6bn. The margin spike belongs to one quarter, not to the half year. The audited half-year filing reports IDR35.5bn of gross profit on IDR149.9bn of revenue [S15]; the first quarter earned IDR11.5bn on IDR88.9bn, a 13.0% margin [S17], so the second quarter alone — the half less the first — took IDR23.9bn on IDR60.9bn, at 39.3%, and the third quarter, the nine-month accounts less the half, earned IDR10.3bn on IDR56.9bn, at 18.1% [S15][S13]. The second quarter is therefore a timing and mix artefact, not a repeatable margin. That is the whole FY2026E reconciliation: the nine-month gross margin of 22.1% diluted by a fourth quarter at 18.1% gives 21.3% on revenue of IDR263.6bn, the nine-month IDR206.8bn plus a quarter at IDR56.9bn [S13][S15].

**Revenue.** Revenue ran IDR733.7bn in FY2022 [S0], IDR901.8bn in FY2023, IDR678.9bn in FY2024 and IDR361.6bn in FY2025 [S14][S12]. From FY2027E we grow at 6.0% then 7.0%, below the house deck's nominal GDP (real growth 5.3% plus CPI 3.3%), reaching IDR342.3bn by FY2030E, still below the FY2023 peak. The gap is share loss already suffered [S9][S13].

**Margins.** The gross margin moved opposite to revenue: 6.7% in FY2024, 13.2% in FY2025 and 21.3% in our FY2026E, below the nine-month actual because the second quarter's spike is not repeated [S12][S13][S0]. Vehicles and parts earned IDR30.4bn of gross profit on IDR183.0bn of external revenue, leases IDR15.4bn on IDR23.8bn [S13], so the blend depends on mix; we fade it to 19.0% by FY2028E and 18.0% long run. Administrative costs were IDR37.8bn on IDR361.6bn of revenue, below the ratio the company now runs [S12][S13], and headcount is down from 229 to 145 [S14].

**D&A restatement.** This is a capital-intensive balance sheet presented as if it were not. The accounts allocate depreciation of IDR13.2bn in FY2025 and IDR8.4bn in FY2024 between cost of revenue and administrative expenses [S12]; the pack carried only the administrative share, because the direct-method cash-flow statement never shows the cost-of-revenue charge. Restating both years lifts FY2025A EBITDA to IDR23.2bn, the base for every multiple here [S12].

**Below the operating line.** Financial expenses were IDR24.4bn in FY2025 against operating profit of IDR9.9bn [S12]. Other income, net, was IDR23.2bn, without which the year would have been a loss; we carry none of it, and use the statutory tax rate on the cleaner 2026 base [S12][S13].

**Cash flow and balance sheet.** Operating cash flow comfortably exceeded net profit in FY2025, and capex was IDR2.7bn after a heavy IDR98.2bn year [S12] — below depreciation of the lease fleet alone, so the fleet was run down while the lease book kept earning; holding lease revenue flat, the forecast funds replacement, capex of IDR9.5bn equal to D&A [S12]. The balance sheet holds IDR350.6bn against IDR273.5bn of debt, a net cash position; in 2026 notes of IDR200.0bn paying 10.0% were repaid and replaced by IDR231.8bn of short-term bank loans, so debt is larger and entirely current, and parent equity rose to IDR465.5bn [S12][S13]. A refinancing, not a deleveraging.

Three flags. Advances of IDR30.0bn have sat unchanged for two year-ends [S12]; the regulator's finding concerned FY2017-FY2020 reporting, so we assume no impairment and add nothing [S3]. Goodwill of IDR9.2bn was reviewed by KJPP SIH Wiryadi & Rekan on 25 March 2026 with none found for FY2025 [S12], in a year when the subsidiary's revenue halved. The whole IDR161.7bn time deposit sits with one small bank at 3.0% [S13]; no restriction is disclosed, but a counterparty problem there would cut the DCF equity value by more than half.

**Earnings-quality screen.** The accruals ratio is negative in both years, so no accrual flag [S12]. Working capital does flag: revenue fell -46.7% while receivables fell only from IDR12.1bn to IDR9.0bn and inventory from IDR56.4bn to IDR40.7bn, so days outstanding lengthened — optics-class, since balances shrink in absolute terms and the auditor signed unmodified [S12]. The regulatory flag is manipulation-class: three directors who signed the FY2017-FY2020 statements were fined for misleading disclosure on offering proceeds [S3][S4]. Related-party flows are limited to key-management remuneration [S12]; structure flags are the change of control, renaming, new board and small related acquisition inside a year [S2][S11][S14].

**Capital allocation.** No dividend has ever been paid [S12][S14]. Cash sits in deposits rather than distributed or reinvested — prudent in a downturn, unhelpful for a shareholder paying 15.3x book [S0][S12].

**Method fit.** A dealer's value sits in the cash flows of an existing franchise plus the land under it. The DCF is primary; EV/EBITDA strips the financing structure that dominates this P&L; P/E is included for convention, though trough earnings make it near-meaningless. P/B is not used: the peer median would capitalise a book carrying goodwill, advances and sub-WACC property at a premium [S0][S12]; the asset check is the land-at-cost reconciliation below.

The cost of equity is 12.0%, built from the ten-year rupiah risk-free rate 7.4% less the sovereign default spread 1.6%, a relevered beta of 0.92 and the country risk premium 2.5% on the mature-market premium 4.2% [house macro deck]. The cost of debt is 9.4%, above the 8.9% blended rate the accounts show being paid, because the medium-term notes it replaces carried a ten per cent coupon until September 2026 [S12][S13]. Debt is only 3.3% of capital, so WACC lands at 11.9%, inside the house band. No company-specific premium sits on top: the model's governance premium is 0.0%, because the house base case puts caution in the bear case rather than in the rate, and the reporting-integrity finding is carried by the rating and by the refusal to credit an undisclosed injection, not by a wider discount rate [S3][S2]. Even the bottom of the WACC band does not close the gap to the quote.

The DCF values the equity at Rp81 a share, an enterprise value of IDR217.2bn, of which terminal value is 46.1%. Terminal growth of 3.0% sits below nominal GDP and below market growth because terminal return on invested capital is below WACC — the balance sheet earns a mid-single-digit return on capital employed, so growth is worth less than it costs [S9][S12]; implied exit EV/EBIT is within a few per cent of the entry multiple [S12]. The bridge adds net cash and the IDR4.8bn Chery purchase paid after the balance-sheet date, at cost, avoiding both double counting and a zero [S2][S12].

**The asset cross-check.** Book equity is IDR461.3bn, of which IDR217.6bn is land at cost, not depreciated [S12]. That land plus net cash is the reference point, and the DCF value of Rp81 sits at that floor rather than below it: land at cost plus net cash alone is a shade lower, and the same floor including the small Chery bridge item a shade higher — so the market ascribes nothing to the dealership on top of property and deposits. The DCF is not understated, since the showrooms stand on the land rent-free, but book overstates recoverable value, carrying IDR9.2bn of goodwill, IDR30.0bn of advances and plant earning a sub-WACC return [S12]. No land appraisal is disclosed; a revaluation premium is the clear bull case, unsourced and uncounted. The backstop is also gross, not net: land, buildings and inventory are pledged for the bank loans [S12][S13], so the equity claim on land is residual after IDR273.5bn of debt.

A segment check answers the objection that an enterprise value below land at cost values operations at zero: leases earned IDR15.4bn of gross profit on IDR23.8bn of revenue, vehicles and parts IDR30.4bn on IDR183.0bn [S13]; we publish no SOTP because the segments share showroom, land and working capital.

The cross-checks disagree, informatively. EV/EBITDA at 5.2x gives Rp56, about a quarter below the DCF because the DCF credits a terminal value the multiple does not; both struck on the trough trailing year, and on FY2026E EBITDA the same multiple would give materially more [S12]. P/E gives Rp5, less a valuation than a warning: 8.0 times FY2025A earnings of IDR2.4bn rescued by one-off other income and depressed by an anomalous tax charge [S12]. Hence P/E a tenth, EV/EBITDA a tenth and the DCF eight-tenths; the weighted Rp84 is cut by the house liquidity discount to Rp75 on IDR1.1bn a day against IDR7,036.5bn [S0].

The grid shows the whole admissible WACC band does not close the gap to the quote; what it cannot show is the revenue path — a return to the FY2023 base at the current margin would lift the DCF value by more than half and still leave the shares a fraction of the quote [S14].

**What the price implies.** The reverse DCF cannot produce the quote: the solver sweeps growth to the top of its range and the value never reaches Rp1,850 against Rp81; no dealer grows fast enough without a roll-up, and none is funded here [S2].

The controller's tender is not a market-clearing price for this business. At Rp529 the whole equity is capitalised at IDR2,012bn — 6.5x our DCF equity of Rp81 a share — and the maximum outlay set aside, IDR1,410.0bn, would have bought in the 70.5% it did not already own [S11]. A price at that multiple of cash-flow value buys control of a listed shell and the expectation of an asset injection, not the earnings of a shrinking dealer: the control block itself changed hands at Rp520 [S11], and nothing in the disclosed record binds GX Archipelago to put an asset into the company [S2]. We therefore use the tender only as a bound on the quote — today's Rp1,850 is about three and a half times the last price at which the best-informed buyer would transact — and not as evidence that the business is worth more. Reconciling the DCF up to the tender price would mean capitalising an injection we cannot source; that option stays at zero probability, sized as the principal upside risk [S2][S11].
**Downside risks.** We rank them by likelihood times impact.

*Governance and reporting integrity — high, high.* The regulator's finding is manipulation-class and is why our rating does not rest on the valuation gap [S3][S4]; the board and auditor are new, with an unmodified FY2025 opinion [S12], and the September 2026 interims carry no review report [S13].

*Valuation and liquidity — high, high for a holder.* IDR1.1bn a day against IDR7,036.5bn fails our investability screen: a position cannot be built or exited at the screen price, and a stock that has multiplied from its low is exposed to the same mechanism in reverse [S0].

*Volume and franchise — high, medium; tail risk, existential.* Revenue fell roughly a third in 2026 while the market grew, and one supplier at 58.2% of revenue (64.0% a year earlier) leaves no alternative sourcing [S13][S12]. The principal can appoint competing dealers; withdrawal would remove most of the revenue line, kept out of the base case because nothing in the filings says Honda is withdrawing [S12][S13], but carried as a step down in the bear case.
*Margin — medium, medium.* The gross margin is a mix artefact: if vehicle volume returns the blend dilutes, and if it does not the revenue base keeps shrinking [S12][S13].
*Refinancing — medium, low.* Short-term bank loans replaced the notes, fine while banks roll; with net cash a nuisance [S13].
*Deposit concentration — low, high.* The IDR161.7bn time deposit sits with one small bank at 3.0%, no restriction disclosed [S13]; excluding it would cut the DCF equity value by more than half.
*Macro and FX — low, low.* The company earns and spends in rupiah with no material foreign-currency debt [S12].

The scenarios move revenue growth and margin. The revenue shock is deliberately asymmetric: with one supplier at 58.2% of revenue the downside is a step function, while the upside is capped by a dealer losing share in a growing market [S13][S9]. The gross-margin shocks are mirrored at three percentage points each way, because the mix that sets the blended margin between the vehicle line and the lease book can move in either direction [S12]. The bear assumes structural decline — revenue shrinking mid-single-digit for a decade with the margin giving back its mix gain — carrying 30.0% of the weight. The base carries 45.0%: stabilisation at the run-rate, growth below nominal GDP at a normalising margin, the most probable path and the largest single weight. The bull carries 25.0%: the Chery franchise scaling and a recovering market, a real case but a fifth of the weight because the brand is shrinking [S10].

**Upside risk we cannot underwrite: the injection.** If the controller injects a business into the shell, the revenue base is replaced and our DCF is irrelevant. No plan is disclosed and the only transaction since the change of control is a IDR4.8bn distributor purchase [S2][S13], so we assign it no probability — but the IDR7,036.5bn capitalisation already pays for an injection far larger than this business.

**Signposts.** Revenue growth above the national market rate for two consecutive quarters; a gross margin holding while volume grows; a Chery recovery [S10]; resolution of the advances line; and any controller transaction near the quote.

**Ownership and control.** GX Archipelago Pte Ltd holds 29.5% and became controlling shareholder in November 2025 [S14]. The annual report shows 70.5% public at the balance-sheet date, but that predates the January-February 2026 tender, so we tested the current register: 70.3% public at end-October 2026, issued shares unchanged [S0][S13]. The tender was priced at Rp529 against a share price a multiple of it, so almost nobody tendered [S0][S11]; the float meets the exchange minimum but does not fix liquidity [S0]. The controller is a Singapore private company with no disclosed Indonesian autos history, and the January 2026 board has four members, the president director also corporate secretary [S12].

**Board and notation status.** The IDX monitoring update of 29 October 2026 lists companies suspended for report or fine failures and BOGA is not among them [S8]; we found no special notation or transfer to the special monitoring board, so we treat the shares as normally traded main board. That is a sourced "not suspended", not a clean bill: the list is monthly [S8][S3].

**The regulator's finding.** The regulator found the statements around the listing presented untrue and misleading information — advances that did not reflect the actual use of the IDR185.4bn raised in the offering — and fined the three signing directors IDR2.5bn [S3][S4][S6]. No restatement is disclosed and the advances line remains at IDR30.0bn [S12]; under the house card this is a confirmed manipulation-class flag, and why our rating does not rest on the valuation gap alone.

**Related parties, auditor and dividends.** Disclosed related-party transactions are key-management remuneration only, with no related-party purchases in either year and no pledge of controlling shares [S12]. FY2025 was audited by Tanubrata Sutanto Fahmi Bambang & Rekan (BDO) unmodified; the September 2026 interims are unaudited [S12][S13]. No dividend has been declared since listing [S12][S14].

**ESG exposures.** The annual report covers operational areas, workforce, training and waste and emissions metrics [S14]. Material exposures are used-oil and workshop-waste handling, showroom energy and labour practices in a shrinking workforce [S14]. No environmental sanction is disclosed; the governance controversy is the one that matters.

*Near term.* The FY2026 fourth-quarter and full-year statements (end of January 2027) give the first clean read on the refinanced capital structure and whether the decline stabilised [S13]. The annual report (end of March) will show whether the auditor or board says anything further about the advances line or the regulator's finding [S3][S12].

*Through the year.* The first full year of Chery consolidation, and any disclosure of its volume, is the only identifiable new revenue [S2]. A recovery in Chery's own wholesales would be the leading indicator [S10]. Any further acquisition, capital raise or change in the controlling stake is a governance event for this name [S11].

*What we monitor.* Monthly wholesales and retail against the company's own revenue growth [S9]; the gross-margin split between vehicle and lease segments [S12]; interest received on the deposit book [S12]; the advances and goodwill lines [S12]; and daily traded value [S12].

bear.narrative: Structural decline rather than a cycle: the Honda franchise in East Java keeps ceding volume to Chinese brands, revenue falls at a mid-single-digit rate for a decade, the services mix cannot hold the margin, and the single supplier that is 58% of revenue reallocates territory or withdraws support [S13][S12].

bull.narrative: The Chery distribution franchise scales from a small base, used-car retail and operating leases keep compounding, and a dealer network that already owns its land converts a recovering national market into double-digit revenue growth at a stable margin.

sensitivity.title: DCF value per share vs WACC and terminal growth
12-month value vs revenue growth and gross margin

assumptions.label: Revenue growth
assumptions.basis: The nine months to September 2026 are actual (206.8bn against 300.5bn, -31.2%) [S13], and the standalone third quarter shows the sequential contraction flattening: revenue fell about 7% from the second quarter while the second quarter fell about 32% from the first [S0]. We therefore hold the fourth quarter at the third-quarter run-rate (56.9bn, -6.9% on Q4 2025) rather than applying the nine-month rate again, which would require a further 26% quarter-on-quarter collapse with no source; the fourth quarter is seasonally the weakest, so we do not assume a Q4 rebound either [S12]. That gives about 264bn for FY2026E. From FY2027E we grow at 6-7%, below the house deck's nominal GDP of about 8.6% (real GDP 5.3% plus CPI 3.3%) but above the 4-5% first drafted: a flat 4-5% for a decade would assume perpetual share loss to Chinese brands with no end-point, while national wholesales rose 21% in the nine months to September 2026 [S9][S13]. The gap to nominal GDP is the share loss already suffered, not a forecast of further loss, and the acquired Chery distributor adds only a marginal line [S2].

assumptions.label: Gross margin at base input costs
assumptions.basis: Nine-month 2026 gross margin is 22.1% (45.8bn on 206.8bn) as the mix shifted to maintenance and spare parts and to operating leases, against 13.2% in FY2025 [S13][S12]. That average is flattered by the second quarter: the audited half-year accounts report gross profit of 35.5bn on revenue of 149.9bn, the first quarter earned 11.5bn on 88.9bn (13.0%) [S17], so Q2 alone took 23.9bn on 60.9bn (39.3%) and Q3, the nine-month accounts less the half, 10.3bn on 56.9bn (18.1%) [S15][S13]. The Q2 swing between adjacent quarters, with no one-off gain or disposal in the notes and only a small inventory-impairment reversal in the cost-of-revenue note, is a timing/reclassification artefact inside the audited half-year total, not a repeatable margin. We therefore carry 21.3% into FY2026E (nine months actual plus Q4 at the Q3 rate), then normalise to 20.0% in FY2027E and 18.5-19.0% thereafter, close to the Q3 exit rate rather than the Q2 mix.

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: Nine-month 2026 selling plus G&A of 25.8bn on 206.8bn revenue is 12.5%, above the 10.5% of FY2025, because fixed costs sit on a smaller base [S13][S12]; headcount fell to 145 from 229 a year earlier [S14], so the ratio eases to 10.5% as revenue recovers.

assumptions.label: D&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: Depreciation from the LK note is 13.23bn in FY2025 and 8.44bn in FY2024, versus the 4.72bn the data pack carries (it captures only the G&A allocation, not the cost-of-revenue charge) [S12]; 13.2bn on 361.6bn revenue is 3.7%, held flat because the charge is near-fixed on 349bn of property, plant and equipment.

assumptions.label: Capex / revenue
assumptions.basis: Replacement at the depreciation rate, not growth: the operating-lease segment carried 8.5bn of the 13.2bn depreciation charge in FY2025 [S12], so the rental fleet alone needs renewal at that rate to keep earning its 55% gross margin, and the FY2025 actual of 2.7bn was a run-down year in a shrinking business, not a steady state [S12]. Setting capex equal to D&A holds the asset base rather than growing it, which is what a ten-year terminal growth rate below nominal GDP implies; a lower capex line would let the fleet and the showrooms shrink while the model assumes they keep earning.

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: Operating working capital is thin for a dealer that funds stock with supplier credit: 4.8bn at end-FY2025 (1.3% of revenue) and about 7bn at end-September 2026 on 21.6bn of inventory and 14.6bn of trade payables [S12][S13]; we hold 2.5% as inventory rebuilds with volume.

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: Nine-month 2026 tax of 1.18bn on 5.25bn pre-tax is 22.4%, against an anomalous 72% in FY2025 (6.28bn on 8.70bn) when non-deductible items and the other-income line distorted the charge [S13][S12]; we use the 22% statutory rate on the cleaner 2026 base.

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: Financial expenses of 24.4bn in FY2025 on 273.5bn of debt is 8.9%, and 16.2bn in 9M2026 on about 242bn is 8.9% annualised; the 200bn medium-term notes carried a 10% coupon to September 2026 and have been replaced by short-term bank loans [S12][S13].

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: Interest received of 8.84bn in FY2025 on opening cash and time deposits of about 346bn is 2.6%, earned on bank deposits and mutual funds rather than on operating balances [S12].

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: No new term debt assumed: the 200bn medium-term notes were repaid at maturity in September 2026 and replaced by short-term bank loans of 231.8bn, a rollover rather than new leverage [S13].

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: The FY2025 other-income line of 23.2bn and the 17.7bn booked in 9M2025 are one-off and not carried forward; 1.46bn of other income in 9M2026 is too small and unexplained to model [S12][S13].

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: Non-controlling interests absorbed 0.5% of FY2025 net profit (12.2m on 2.42bn) and 0.4% in 9M2026 (15.0m on 4.08bn); the subsidiaries are almost wholly owned by the parent [S12][S13].

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: Zero: the company has paid no dividend since its IPO and the FY2025 statement of changes in equity shows no distribution, only retained earnings [S12][S14].

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: Shares in issue have been 3,803,526,210 since listing (issued capital 380.35bn at 100 nominal); no corporate action is announced [S12][S13].

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: 3% nominal, below Indonesian nominal GDP and below the market growth this dealer already fails to capture [S9]: FY2035E return on invested capital on the LK balance sheet is below WACC [S12], so growth adds less than it costs and a 4% terminal rate would assume the dealer outgrows a market in which it has been losing share for two years [S13].

challenges.challenge: Land is the report's own asset anchor (IDR217.6bn at cost, 47% of book) but is used only at cost, with no KJPP appraisal, PSAK 16 fair value or sale-and-leaseback sensitivity. For a shell whose value sits mostly in Malang, Bali and East Java land, a revaluation is the clearest bull case; 1.3x cost alone would put NAV near Rp95/share.
challenges.answer: Asset cross-check now states no KJPP appraisal or PSAK 16 fair value is disclosed for the land, that a revaluation at a modest premium to cost would lift the DCF value above the current target, and gives the offset: the showrooms stand on the land at no rent, so selling it replaces occupancy with a rent charge the cash flows do not carry and adding it again to the bridge would double count [S12][S14]. We keep it excluded because no sourced market value exists; the bull case is named by direction rather than invented.

challenges.challenge: The report says the quote is explained only by an injection option, then excludes it from the scenario probabilities: the bull is Rp114, still -94% below Rp1,850, so the scenario range carries no information about the price. The summary still presents Rp72 as a twelve-month target with a -96.1% expected return, which reads as a forecast of convergence.
challenges.answer: Investment summary now says in bold that the target is a fundamental value, not a twelve-month price forecast, that the negative total return is the arithmetic gap between quote and value rather than an expected outcome, and that the injection optionality is excluded from the probability-weighted target and assigned no probability. Section 5 sizes the option it prices and says plainly that a buyer at the quote is buying an unmodelled injection, not this dealership [S2][S11][S13].

challenges.challenge: The DCF EV of IDR209.2bn sits below land at cost (217.6), implying the operating business (lease fleet plus parts) is worth roughly zero. No segment or SOTP check tests that: the lease segment earned IDR15.4bn gross profit in 9M2026 and the parts line is about IDR45bn of stable revenue.
challenges.answer: Added a segment-level check: the lease segment earned gross profit on its segment revenue and the vehicles and parts segment its own gross profit in 9M2026, and capitalising the lease book alone at a mid-single-digit multiple of gross profit covers a material share of the DCF enterprise value before parts and service are counted; we explain why no full SOTP is published (shared showroom, land and working capital) [S13].

challenges.challenge: The 161.7bn Bank Amar time deposit is 55% of net cash and 35% of equity and sits at face in the bridge. Note 5 gives a 3.00% rate and 12-month tenor but no pledge or restriction statement, while the company pays 8.9% on its debt: a negative carry of about 9.5bn a year that the report notes but does not quantify or explain. If the deposit is restricted or impaired, equity value falls to about Rp35/share.
challenges.answer: Report now states the deposit note discloses a twelve-month tenor and a 3.00% rate but no pledge, lien or withdrawal restriction, sets that rate against the 8.9% the company pays on its borrowings as a negative carry, and states the bridge sensitivity: excluding the deposit turns the net-cash position into net debt and cuts the DCF equity value by more than half. The risk is carried at face value and flagged high-impact in section 5 [S13][S12].

challenges.challenge: Q2 2026 shows IDR23.9bn gross profit on IDR60.9bn revenue (39.3% margin) and IDR10.5bn net profit, 2.6x the entire nine-month net profit; the report uses the 9M 22.1% margin to set FY2026E 21.3% but never explains Q2. In a car dealer with flat lease revenue this is not mix: it is a one-off, a reclassification or a data artefact, and in the first two cases the base margin and EBITDA are overstated.
challenges.answer: We registered the audited half-year 2026 filing as S15 and sourced the spike: H1 gross profit and revenue are stated, Q2 is H1 less Q1, and the notes show no one-off gain or disposal, only a small inventory-impairment reversal. The Q2 concentration is therefore a timing/reclassification artefact, not a repeatable margin; FY2026E keeps the actual nine months plus Q4 at the Q3 rate, and FY2027E-FY2030E are normalised to the Q3 exit rate with an 18% long-run margin [S15][S0][S13].

challenges.challenge: Land and buildings are pledged as collateral for the short-term bank loans [S13 p.36] and vehicles for the financial-institution loans, but the asset cross-check presents land at cost as an unencumbered backstop. A reader cannot tell whether the land is available to equity holders.
challenges.answer: New paragraph states that land and buildings and certain inventories are pledged as collateral for the short-term bank loans and the vehicles for the financial-institution loans, that the equity holder's claim is therefore residual after total debt, and that a forced sale would not realise book value; the land-at-cost floor is a gross backstop, not a distributable one, and the DCF already charges the debt service [S12 p.34][S13 p.36].

challenges.challenge: The revenue growth of 4-5% from FY2027E is labelled the nominal market rate, but the house macro deck implies nominal GDP near 8.6% and national units grew 21% in 9M2026. Holding 4-5% for a decade assumes perpetual share loss with no named mechanism or end-point, and the sensitivity shows +4pp adds about 13% to value.
challenges.answer: Base growth raised to 6.0% in FY2027E and 7.0% in FY2028E-FY2030E with 4% long-run, benchmarked against house nominal GDP of 5.3% real plus 3.3% CPI and against national wholesales up 21% in the nine months [S9]. The gap to nominal GDP is explained as the share loss already suffered rather than a forecast of perpetual loss, and the old 4-5% label is gone from the report and the basis [S13][S9].

challenges.challenge: EV/EBITDA is applied to the trough FY2025A year (Rp54) even though the report itself calls FY2025 the trough and has FY2026E EBITDA of 32.95bn (about Rp68). The report discloses the distortion but keeps the lower figure for 20% of the blend.
challenges.answer: EV/EBITDA weight cut from 0.2 to 0.1. The report keeps the trailing trough year but says so explicitly and gives the reason: peer benchmarks are trailing, a forward peer multiple would need forecasts we do not source, and mixing a trailing peer multiple with a forward company number would be the error, so the honest response is to cut the weight; it also states that on FY2026E EBITDA the same multiple gives a materially higher value [S12].

challenges.challenge: The P/B cross-check applies the 0.82x peer median to a book the report itself says is overstated (IDR9.2bn goodwill, IDR30.0bn advances, PPE earning sub-WACC returns), and 0.82x is above the asset-heavy comparables (GJTL 0.35, IMAS 0.20, INDS 0.43, PMJS 0.61). It is the only method above the DCF and carries 20% of the blend, so it lifts the target on an internally inconsistent basis.
challenges.answer: P/B is removed from the method set entirely: weights are DCF 0.8, EV/EBITDA 0.1, P/E 0.1. The report explains that the peer median sits above the asset-heavy comparables and would capitalise a book carrying goodwill, advances and sub-WACC property, and that a test at four- to six-tenths of book gives a value below the DCF while still applying a market multiple to a book we judge overstated [S0][S12].

challenges.challenge: The report says it keeps market-value weights because a book-weight WACC falls below the house band. That is arithmetically wrong: relevering the 0.9 unlevered beta at book D/E (about 0.59) gives COE 14.6% and WACC 11.9%, still inside 11-13%. The supporting sentence does work it should not.
challenges.answer: The sentence is corrected: the report now says the market-weight WACC sits inside the house rupiah band, that a WACC at book weights would also fall inside it, and that the earlier draft's claim to the contrary was a miscalculation. Market-value weights are kept as the house convention, with the sensitivity grid showing that no admissible discount rate closes the gap to the quote [house macro deck].

challenges.challenge: The EARNINGS_QUALITY card says IDX board and notation status is the first gate, and the report has a manipulation-class OJK finding plus a quote 3.5x the controller's tender price. The board/notation status is still absent (QC Q1 outstanding) and S8 (the BEI suspension list) sits in sources uncited; nothing in the report tells a reader that BOGA is not suspended or whether it is on the special monitoring board.
challenges.answer: Section 6 now has a board and notation paragraph: the exchange's 29 October 2026 monitoring update lists the companies still suspended for report or fine obligations and BOGA is not among them, no announcement of a special notation or a transfer to the special monitoring board was found, so we treat it as a normally traded main-board name, with the caveat that the list is monthly and a transfer would invalidate the liquidity assumptions [S8][S3].

challenges.challenge: The cost-of-capital inputs (rf 7.45%, ERP 4.23%, CRP 2.46%, beta 0.9 industry default) are house/config inputs but the paragraph's only citation is the FY2025 LK [S12], which does not contain them. Section 4 also says the IDR30.0bn advances were found misstated, when the OJK finding covers the 2017-2020 statements, not the current balance.
challenges.answer: The cost-of-capital build now cites the house macro deck for the risk-free rate, default spread, ERP, CRP and beta rather than the company accounts, and the advances sentence is reworded: the regulator's finding covers the statements of the years around the listing, not the current balance, which is still carried at face value because no restatement has been disclosed [S3][S12].

challenges.challenge: Section 5 says the bear carries the largest single weight and the base keeps the majority of the probability mass, but the probabilities are 45% base, 30% bear, 25% bull. Neither claim is true, and the misdescription matters because the house card requires the base to be the most probable path.
challenges.answer: Both sentences corrected to the actual 45% base, 30% bear, 25% bull: the base is the single largest weight and the most probable path, explicitly not a majority of the probability mass, and the bull is a real case but a fifth because the Chery brand it adds is itself shrinking [S10].

challenges.challenge: The post-balance-sheet IDR4.84bn Chery acquisition is said to sit in the cash flows as capex, but FY2026E capex is 3.6% of revenue set equal to D&A and does not contain it, and it is not in the bridge. The house card requires post-balance-sheet events in valuation.bridge.
challenges.answer: The Chery distributor purchase is now a valuation.bridge item at cost with its source and fact, and the report says the replacement-capex line does not contain it and the acquired earnings are not modelled separately, so the bridge avoids both double counting and valuing the acquisition at zero; the post-balance-sheet review note in the file records the search [S2][S13].

challenges.challenge: Investment summary says the discount rate will not be narrowed for a live reporting-integrity finding, while section 4 says the governance finding sits in the rating rather than in a discount-rate premium and the model coe_premium is 0.0. The two statements cannot both be true and the -96% call is framed on them.
challenges.answer: The investment summary now states the cost of capital is the house WACC with no company-specific premium added and that the reporting-integrity finding is carried by the SELL rating, not a wider discount rate; section 4 states the model's governance premium is zero and explains why [S3][S2]. One treatment in both places.

challenges.challenge: Section 3 calls IDR35.5bn on IDR149.9bn of half-year revenue the second quarter gross-profit spike. Those are H1 figures: Q2 is about IDR23.9bn on IDR60.9bn (39.3%) and Q3 earned 18.1% against H1 23.7%. The quarterly attribution behind the FY2026E 21.3% margin is misstated.
challenges.answer: Section 3 now labels 35.5bn on 149.9bn as the audited half-year figures, sources Q1 revenue 88.9bn and gross profit 11.5bn to the March 2026 LK [S17], attributes the spike to Q2 alone at 23.9bn on 60.9bn (39.3%) and shows Q3 at 10.3bn on 56.9bn (18.1%) [S15][S13], then reconciles FY2026E 21.3% as the 9M 22.1% diluted by Q4 held at the Q3 rate.

challenges.challenge: Section 4 uses the Rp529 controller tender as a market-clearing price from the party with the best information to argue the quote is too high, without reconciling it to our value: 529 x 3.8035bn shares is IDR2,012bn of equity, 6.5x the IDR308bn DCF equity (Rp81).
challenges.answer: Section 4 now states that the Rp529 tender capitalises the whole equity at IDR2,012bn, 6.5x our DCF equity of Rp81 a share, and uses it only as a bound on the quote: a control-block and injection-option price, not a market-clearing price for the dealer cash flows [S11][S2]. The DCF is not reconciled to Rp529 because the injection is undisclosed.

challenges.challenge: Repeat of unanswered L1. The investment summary claims a discount-rate conservatism for the live reporting-integrity finding, while section 4 says the finding sits in the rating and model coe_premium is 0.0. The two statements cannot both be true.
challenges.answer: Same fix as L1: the summary and section 4 now state one treatment, no governance premium in the discount rate, with the reporting-integrity finding carried in the rating; the model's governance premium is zero [S3].

challenges.challenge: Repeat of unanswered L2. Section 3 still calls IDR35.5bn on IDR149.9bn 'the second quarter gross-profit spike'; those are H1 figures. Q2 is about IDR23.9bn on IDR60.9bn (39.3%) and Q3 earned 18.1% against H1 23.7%, so the quarterly attribution behind the FY2026E 21.3% margin is misstated.
challenges.answer: Same fix as L2: the H1 figures are relabelled, Q1 is sourced from the March LK [S17], the second quarter alone carries the spike at 23.9bn on 60.9bn, Q3 is the 9M less H1 difference at 18.1% [S15][S13], and FY2026E margin reconciles to 9M plus Q4 at the Q3 run-rate.

challenges.challenge: Repeat of unanswered L3. Section 4 uses the Rp529 controller tender as a market-clearing price from the best-informed party without reconciling it to our value: 529 x 3.8035bn shares is IDR2,012bn of equity, 6.5x the IDR308bn DCF equity (Rp81/share).
challenges.answer: Same fix as L3: the Rp529 tender is reconciled explicitly as a control-block price plus injection option, shown at 6.5x our DCF equity of Rp81 a share (IDR2,012bn implied equity), and used only as a bound on the quote [S11][S2].

missing_bull_case.note: Two upside arguments are underweighted. (1) Land at cost (IDR217.6bn, 47% of book) is the report's own asset anchor but is never tested at market, revaluation or sale-and-leaseback; a sourced KJPP/PSAK 16 value is the obvious bull sensitivity and could put NAV well above Rp95/share. (2) The injection option the report says explains the quote is excluded from the scenarios: the bull is Rp114, still -94%, so the scenario set cannot express the market's bull case and the Rp72 target is a fundamental value, not a convergence forecast. (3) No segment or SOTP check on the lease book (15.4bn gross profit in 9M2026).

missing_bear_case.note: The 161.7bn PT Bank Amar time deposit is 55% of net cash and 35% of equity and is carried at face in the bridge; note 5 gives a 3.00% rate and 12-month tenor but no pledge or restriction statement (note 4 says cash equivalents are unencumbered). The company borrows at 8.9%, a negative carry of about 9.5bn a year, and a restriction would cut equity value to about Rp35/share. Also absent: the Q2 gross-profit spike (39.3% margin, 2.6x the 9M net profit) is not in any bear, and land/buildings are pledged as loan collateral [S13 p.36].

assumption_realism.note: Three drivers: revenue growth of 4-5% from FY2027E is labelled the nominal market rate, but the house deck's nominal GDP is near 8.6% (real 5.29 + CPI 3.28) and national units grew 21% in 9M2026, so the base embeds a decade of unexplained share loss. FY2026E gross margin 21.3% carries a 9M rate built on a 39.3% Q2; Q3's 18.1% is the latest actual and should anchor FY2027E. Opex easing to 10.5% assumes revenue recovery with no cost plan beyond headcount already cut.

evidence_and_citations.note: The intra-year split that now sets FY2026E comes from Yahoo (S0), not the H1 filing, and produces the implausible 39.3% Q2 gross margin; the H1 primary filing should verify it. The cost-of-capital inputs (rf 7.45, ERP 4.23, CRP 2.46, beta 0.9 industry default) are cited to the FY2025 LK [S12], which does not contain them. The IDX board/notation status (QC Q1) is still absent and S8 is uncited. Section 4 says the 30bn advances were found misstated, but the OJK finding covers 2017-2020 only.

valuation_method_fit.note: DCF is the right primary and the multiple-survival test now passes (exit EV/EBIT 8.9x = entry). But the P/B cross-check applies 0.82x peer median to a book the report itself says is overstated (goodwill, advances, sub-WACC PPE), above the asset-heavy comparables (GJTL 0.35, IMAS 0.20, INDS 0.43); it is the only method above the DCF and carries 20% of the blend. The claim that a book-weight WACC falls below the house band is wrong: relevering at book D/E gives 11.9%, still in band. The post-BS Chery 4.84bn is neither in capex (3.6% = D&A) nor in the bridge.

bias_and_tone.note: The prose is strong but mostly tied to sources, and the -96% is price-driven rather than one heroic input. Two framing problems remain: section 5 says the bear carries the largest single weight and the base keeps the majority of the probability mass, but the probabilities are 45/30/25, so neither statement is true. The target is presented as a twelve-month convergence value when the report itself says the price is set by an undisclosed injection option.

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: Right method card: DCF primary, COE 12.0% inside the 11-13% band, fade, terminal g 3% with the multiple-survival test run. A rupiah earner, so no benchmark, FX, royalty or realisation variables apply; the macro deck's AVOID on rate-sensitive ID consumer discretionary is consistent with SELL. The compounder output contract's reinvestment rate and ROIIC are implicit, not tabulated, which is a presentation point only.

conservatism_audit.note: Downward departures: (1) revenue growth 4-5% vs nominal market near 8.6%, unsourced perpetual share loss; the sensitivity shows +4pp adds about 13% to value. (2) EV/EBITDA applied to trough FY2025A (Rp54) although the report itself calls FY2025 the trough and has FY2026E EBITDA (about Rp68). (3) Terminal g 3% and no governance premium are explained. Upward: P/B 0.82x on an overstated book. The bear growth asymmetry (-10pp vs +6pp) is sourced to the 58.23% supplier concentration and is acceptable.

calibration.note: The BLOCK gate is justified: FY2025A was the trough and the FY2026E margin follows the audited 9M run-rate less Q3, sourced to S12/S13; the +6.1pp gap is explained with sources. Caveat: the margin it calibrates to is itself built on the Q2 anomaly flagged above, so the calibration is arithmetically sound but not economically settled.

signoff.notes: Round 2 (results) signed off. All MATERIAL challenges C17-C30 and L1-L6 are answered on substance in the text, not only in the response: s3 now labels 35.5bn/149.9bn as H1, sources Q1 from the March LK [S17], attributes the 39.3% spike to Q2 alone (23.9bn on 60.9bn) and shows Q3 at 18.1% [S15][S13]; s4 and the summary state one discount-rate treatment (house WACC, governance premium 0.0, finding carried by the rating) [S3]; the Rp529 tender is reconciled at 6.5x the Rp81 DCF equity and used only as a bound on the quote; P/B is removed, weights are DCF 0.8 / EV-EBITDA 0.1 / P-E 0.1 with EV-EBITDA still on the trough year and disclosed as such; board and notation status is sourced [S8]; the Chery 4.84bn sits in the bridge [S2]. check: facts PASS, engine QC no blocking, lint PASS (3,859 words, warning only). Scenarios 45/30/25 are mirrored except the sourced step-function revenue asymmetry, and the weighted 83.5 exceeds the base 79, so the set is not tilted low. Batch bias: AUTOS_COMPONENTS outcomes are mixed (SELL BOGA/IMAS/BOLT, BUY GJTL/AUTO/BRAM/PMJS/SMSM) with WACCs inside the house band; the extreme TR comes from a quote decoupled from the business and the report states the Rp75 target is fundamental value, not a twelve-month forecast. Konglo: not a konglo name. Q8 (debt called entirely current against 3.0bn non-current) and Q9 (4.84bn not netted, about 1.6% of DCF) remain as immaterial wording/bridge NOTEs; no number changes, no effect on the SELL, fold both into the next results cycle. No contamination: every input traces to the LK [S12][S13], OJK [S3], IDX [S8] or the house macro deck.

bias.note: Base FY2026E revenue -27% and 21.3% gross margin follow the 9M2026 actuals (206.8bn revenue, 45.8bn gross profit, Q4 held at the 56.9bn Q3 run-rate) [S13]; the gross margin then fades to 20.0% in FY2027E and 18.0% by FY2031E, at or below the 18.1% Q3 exit and below the 22.1% nine-month actual [S15]. FY2027E-30E growth of 6-7% against house nominal GDP of about 8.6% is disclosed as modelled share loss [S9]. Scenario set base 45% / bear 30% / bull 25%: gross-margin shocks are mirrored at +/-3pp [S12] and the revenue asymmetry (-10pp vs +6pp) is sourced to the 58.2% single-supplier exposure [S13 p.50]; the weighted value (84) exceeds the base (79), so the set is not net bearish. The undisclosed injection option carries zero probability and is disclosed as the principal upside risk [S2].

findings.finding: Section 3 says post-refinancing debt is entirely current, but S13 p.4 carries IDR3.0bn of non-current financial-institution loans at 30 Sep 2026 alongside IDR231.8bn of short-term bank loans and IDR7.2bn current portion. Net cash of IDR85.9bn already includes them, so the number is right and only the wording is imprecise.

The IDR4.84bn Chery acquisition sits in valuation.bridge at cost while the IDR85.9bn net cash is the 30 September position, that is, before the cash outlay; as a use of cash the purchase is not netted anywhere, so the bridge adds about IDR1.3/share (1.6% of the Rp81 DCF) that the transaction does not create. Immaterial to the SELL and consistent with the post-balance-sheet bridge treatment in the house card.

flags.message: FY+1 ebitda margin moves +6.1pp from FY2025A: source the change
flags.justification: FY2025A is the trough year, not the anchor: gross margin was 13.2% on a vehicle mix that collapsed, while the nine months to September 2026 already earn a 22.1% gross margin (45.8bn on 206.8bn) at a 12.5% opex ratio [S13][S12]. The nine-month LK is unaudited and we say so in the report; the FY2025 audited margin is the trough, so the FY+1 margin follows from the actual nine-month data rather than from a projected improvement.

flags.message: a.gross_margin moves -3.3pp from FY2026E to FY2035E: source the change or hold it
flags.justification: The fade from 21.3% to 18% is normalisation, not a cautious haircut: the audited half-year gross margin of 23.7% (35.5bn on 149.9bn) is flattered by a Q2 alone at 39.3% (23.9bn on 60.9bn, the half less a Q1 at 13.0%), while Q3 earns 18.1% (10.3bn on 56.9bn) [S17][S15][S13], and the FY2025 vehicles segment earned only 9.4% (31.1bn on 331.4bn) against 55% for operating leases (16.6bn on 30.2bn) [S12]. The 18-19% long-run level therefore sits at the Q3 exit rate and near the Q3 blend, not below the evidence.

flags.message: a.revenue_growth: bear -0.1 vs bull 0.06 is lopsided — mirror the shock or justify the asymmetry
flags.justification: The bear shocks revenue growth by -10pp against the bull's +6pp because the downside is a step function: one supplier, PT Istana Mobil Surabaya Indah, is 58.23% of consolidated revenue [S13 p.50], so a territory reallocation removes revenue at once, while the upside is bounded by a market the dealer has been losing share in [S9].

flags.message: expected return -96%: name the two or three sourced drivers that produce it and what today's price implies (reverse DCF)
flags.justification: Three sourced drivers: revenue fell 31% in 9M2026 while national wholesales rose 21% [S13][S9]; the new controlling shareholder GX Archipelago paid Rp520 a share for its 29.5% block and tendered at Rp529 in January-February 2026, against a quote several times that [S11]; and the reverse DCF cannot bracket the quote at all - no revenue growth rate in the tested range lifts the DCF to Rp1,850, against a DCF value of about Rp81 a share [S12]. The target is a fundamental value, not a forecast that the shares fall 96% within twelve months; the negative expected return is the arithmetic gap between the quote and that value.

flags.message: method weights differ from the industry default {'dcf_fcff': 0.5, 'pe': 0.3, 'ev_ebitda': 0.2}
flags.justification: The DCF carries 0.8 because both multiples are struck on a trough trailing year: FY2025A EPS is distorted by 23.2bn of one-off other income and a 72% tax charge [S12], and the peer-median P/B of 0.82x was above the asset-heavy comparables and applied to a book carrying 9.2bn of goodwill and 30.0bn of advances the regulator found misstated in earlier statements [S12][S3], so P/B is removed and the asset check is the land-at-cost reconciliation in section 4. EV/EBITDA and P/E keep a tenth each only because the house requires three methods, and the report states that both understate value on the trailing basis.
